A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same TRACE study and support direct comparison of the supplied text, equations, figures and tables. Both reference Appendices B–E, but neither includes those appendices or embedded attachments. The judgments below concern the supplied content; the referenced appendix material cannot be compared.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original defense evaluations on three datasets, including benchmark results, component ablations and adaptive-attack experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 2–3 and Figures 8–10, alongside the empirical analyses supporting TRACE.

M1.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 retain the same contextual and focal transformations, SSIM filtering, variance-based scoring and thresholded inference. No method component or procedure changes in the supplied content.

E1.justification: Section 6 and Table 2 retain MS-COCO, PASCAL VOC and Synthesized Traffic Signs, with the same seven backdoor attacks. No represented dataset, task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same five comparison defenses: TeCo, Detector Cleanse, Strip, FreqDetector and SCALE-UP. Their participation, including FreqDetector's unavailable CIB entries, is unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented detector configurations, F1/AUROC metrics and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Section 6.2 retains b = 30, f = 50 and the SSIM threshold of 0.1; Table 3 uses the same adaptive-attack weights.

E4.justification: The supplied component ablations, query-count and threshold sensitivity analyses, explanatory case studies and adaptive-attack tests remain unchanged in Figures 7–10 and Table 3. The referenced supplementary analyses are absent from both files.

E5.justification: Section 6.1 retains the same standard-deviation reporting across backdoors: F1 0.880 ± 0.040 and AUROC 0.897 ± 0.041. These are not seed-based uncertainty estimates; no repeated-run, seed or statistical-reporting change is documented.

E6.justification: The supplied numerical tables, plotted results and qualitative findings match. For example, TRACE's MS-COCO/YOLO averages remain F1 0.877 and AUROC 0.900 in Table 2, and Table 3's adaptive-attack results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The supplied attack formalization, threat-model assumptions, Definitions 1–2, Equations 1–6 and adaptive-loss expression are unchanged. No formal result or proof is added to the available pages; the referenced Appendix E cannot be assessed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same black-box, attack-agnostic TRACE contribution, anomalous transformation-consistency observations, claimed 30% AUROC improvement and resistance to adaptive attacks.

C2.justification: The supplied explanations involving contextual bias, shortcut learning, regression continuity and the Island Effect are unchanged. Section 7 retains the limitations of transformation overhead and reliance on auxiliary public data.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit GitHub code-access link to the abstract, absent from v1. This adds reproducibility information without documenting an implementation or experimental-setting change; repository availability and contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the 52-entry reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. Changed citation back-reference page numbers reflect text reflow. The referenced extended related work in Appendix B is unavailable in both files.

P1.justification: v2 consolidates the Huazhong University affiliations, replaces the contact email and adds the code-availability sentence. The author list, section structure and remaining scientific prose are retained.

P2.justification: The shorter affiliation block and added abstract sentence produce limited reflow in the early pages and references. All ten figures and three tables retain their substantive content, design and numbering.

improvement.justification: Within the supplied PDFs, the new code pointer modestly improves implementation-access and reproducibility documentation. Scientific evidence and conclusions remain unchanged. The benefit is limited: the referenced appendices remain missing, and the PDFs do not establish the repository's availability or completeness.
